description: Fetch the full record for one exact OEM part number: specs, description, verification, every source URL, and fitted models. Use get_part_fits instead when you only need the list of models it fits. Use check_part_fits instead for yes/no against specific models (or several part numbers at once). Use search_parts instead for keyword/fuzzy text. Use resolve_request instead for a vague repair need. Matching order: exact number, then ignoring case/dashes/spaces, then leading zeros, then retired numbers (returns the current record with a superseded note). Several matches return status ambiguous with candidates. Not found is an error result (LPF has no document, not incompatibility).

client.description: Optional: your agent or app name (letters and digits), used only for anonymous usage counts.

part_number.description: Required. OEM part number (FRU, spare or Dell P/N), with or without dashes or spaces, e.g. "01FR025", "7K4PW", "L78555-005".

name: get_part

display_name.description: Short human label; not an identifier

fit_status.description: no_documented_fit: there is no fit or no result: LPF has no OEM document for it. Never means incompatible. not_asserted: a did-you-mean suggestion; no fit claim is made.

outcome.description: Always present. One field to branch on for every tool: found | no_documented_fit (identified, but no OEM-documented fit; never means incompatible) | needs_clarification (ask the user; see clarifying_question/candidates) | not_found (nothing LPF covers matches). Full contract: /api/states
